page.layout: One printed page, single text column with a rule and a heading below the text. Running head at top with page number at left. Main text runs down the right side of the scan. A numeral line set centred between paragraphs. Ornamental rule below the text, then heading, then body text in a new section. Catchword at lower right.

main_text.p: si tria,triginta,& sic deinceps. Si tertio loco duo fuerint: designant ducenta, si tria, trecenta. Si quarto loco duo fuerint: designat duo millia,si tria,tria millia,&c.
Observandum quoque propter pronun-tiandi facilitatem,ut sub quarto quoq; charactere punctus notetur, qui millenarium denotabit numerum, hoc modo:
Exemplum dictum sic Latini eloquuntur: Millies millena millia, ducentiestri-cies quater millena millia, quinquaginta sexaginta septem millia, octingenta nona-ginta.
Hactenus de Notatione dictum: sequitur Numeratio.
main_text.head: Quid est Numeratio?
main_text.p: EST qua ex oblatis numerorum termi-nis alius invenitur. Illud autem sum-mopere observandum, ut numerus alius sub alio directe scribatur: nec quicquam refert si non omnes numerorum termini aeque multas habeant notas, modo notae aliae sub aliis directe notentur.
Numerationis species sunt quatuor: Ad-ditio,Subductio, Multiplicatio,& Divisio.

page.notes: Dots below the numeral line (under the 1 and the 0 and between 6 and 7 area) are printed points marking the millenary sign; not transcribed as text. Ornamental rule above the heading is a printed decoration. The catchword "Quid" is italic and underlined. Possible printing variants: "ducenties tri-cies" reads as ducentiestri-cies at the line break; the printed hyphen is kept.
